title: Reported Speech in Depth
summary: Handle tense backshift, pronoun changes, time references, and reported commands with precision.

sections.heading: Backshift as perspective
sections.body: Backshift is not mechanical; it depends on whether the original statement is still presented from the past perspective. In careful reporting, present often becomes imperfect and future becomes conditional.

examples.pt: Ana disse que morava em Campinas.
examples.en: Ana said that she lived in Campinas.

examples.pt: Ana disse que mora em Campinas.
examples.en: Ana said that she lives in Campinas.
examples.note: possible if the speaker emphasizes it is still true

sections.heading: Deixis: here, now, tomorrow
sections.body: Words tied to the original situation often change: **aqui → ali/lá**, **hoje → naquele dia**, **amanhã → no dia seguinte**, **ontem → no dia anterior**.

examples.pt: Ele falou que chegaria no dia seguinte.
examples.en: He said he would arrive the next day.

examples.pt: Ela disse que não ficaria ali.
examples.en: She said she would not stay there.

sections.heading: Commands, requests, and advice
sections.body: Reported commands often use **mandar**, **pedir**, **recomendar**, or **aconselhar** with **para + infinitive** or **que + subjunctive**.

examples.pt: O médico pediu para eu descansar.
examples.en: The doctor asked me to rest.

examples.pt: Ela recomendou que nós chegássemos cedo.
examples.en: She recommended that we arrive early.

examples.pt: Meu chefe mandou entregar o relatório hoje.
examples.en: My boss ordered the report to be delivered today.

keyPoints: Backshift reflects reporting perspective, not a rigid rule.
Time and place words often shift in indirect speech.
Reported requests use pedir para + infinitive or pedir que + subjunctive.

commonMistakes.right: Ele disse que chegaria no dia seguinte.
commonMistakes.note: From a past reporting perspective, shift future and time reference.
Aqui usually shifts to ali/lá in reported speech.
